title: Abu Dhabi scientists use AI to develop pain killer 'more effective than morphine'
key_facts: Insilico Medicine, a clinical-stage biotechnology company with scientists in Abu Dhabi's Masdar City, used AI to develop a pill called ISM9528 for acute and chronic pain.
The company believes it could be more effective than morphine and could be an alternative to opioids, reducing dependence risk.
It has shown promising results in preclinical (before human) studies; the next step is to test it on humans.
Alex Aliper, president and co-founder, called a non-opioid candidate outperforming morphine in preclinical models "unprecedented" and said the profile was "very clean" on several species.
Health experts say nine out of 10 potential drugs that reach human testing fail to be approved.
Insilico says AI cuts the time to nominate a preclinical candidate to about 12 to 18 months versus about five years; clinical trials can still take about a decade.
The Abu Dhabi team is also at an early stage on a cancer drug including for glioblastoma.
quote_evidence: “To see a non-opioid candidate outperform morphine in preclinical models is unprecedented,” Alex Aliper, president and co-founder of the company, told The National.
Nine out of 10 potential drugs that reach the human testing stage fail to be approved, health experts say.
But AI does not shorten the human trial process, the company added.
why_it_matters_hint: A safe non-addictive painkiller would matter to many patients, but it is early and company-reported.
notes: All performance claims come from Insilico; no published data cited; the article's first paragraphs contain garbled wording ("promising during results initial trials") so only the clear statements are used.
